name: anon-rpc example (Firefox)
description: Minimal Firefox MV3 extension that answers RPC through a hash-pinned anon-rpc worker, hosted in its background page.
//browser_specific_settings: 140 is the oldest Firefox this was measured on (ESR). The isolation comes from the iframe's sandbox attribute, which Firefox has long supported.
//background: Firefox's MV3 background is an event page with a DOM, so it holds the sandboxed iframe itself. No offscreen document — Firefox has none and needs none.
//host_permissions: For the background page's fetch of the worker bundle, which is hash-verified (§4). The worker's own fetches do NOT use these: it runs at a null origin.
//sandbox: Firefox 154+ honours this, but measured on 140 and 157, Firefox applies no CSP inside an extension frame that carries the iframe sandbox attribute — and §6 requires that attribute. The policy below is declared so the page is right if Firefox starts applying it; the attribute's opaque origin is the boundary today.

content_security_policy.//sandbox: As on Chrome, plus data: in script-src: Firefox refuses importScripts(blob:) in an opaque-origin worker, so the harness loads the bundle from a data: URL there. 'wasm-unsafe-eval' is for worker bundles compiled to WebAssembly. No 'unsafe-eval' or 'unsafe-inline' is needed.
content_security_policy.sandbox: sandbox allow-scripts; script-src 'self' blob: data: 'wasm-unsafe-eval'; worker-src blob:; connect-src *;
